# ferriskey_authz_schema (Resource)

Manages the Cedar schema of a FerrisKey realm (singleton per realm). The schema must declare its types and actions inside its `namespace` (default `App`, never `FerrisKey`) and is merged server-side with the built-in schema (see the `ferriskey_authz_builtin_schema` data source). The API refuses a schema that makes an enabled policy or template invalid, so create policies after the schema and update them before narrowing it. The API has **no delete endpoint** for schemas: destroying this resource only removes it from Terraform state and leaves the schema stored on the server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ferriskey_authz_schema" "main" {
  realm     = "acme"
  namespace = "App"

  source = <<-EOT
    namespace App {
      entity Doc;
      action read appliesTo { principal: [FerrisKey::User], resource: [Doc] };
    }
  EOT
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `realm` (String) Realm whose schema is managed. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `source` (String) Cedar schema text (the realm's own schema, without the built-in types). Stored and returned verbatim.

### Optional

- `namespace` (String) Cedar namespace the schema declares its types in. A Cedar identifier other than `FerrisKey`. Defaults to `App` server-side.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier (equal to `realm`).
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp of the last schema replacement, as reported by the API.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ferriskey_authz_schema.main acme
```
